newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices close up despite weak earnings.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices close up despite weak earnings.

text.p: China's stock markets overcame a string of weak corporate results to end stronger on Wednesday, with investors shrugging off bad earnings issued by listed firms at the end of the 1996 reporting season, brokers said.
Analysts said investors had widely expected some of the results to be poor.
The Shanghai B share index surged 1.863 points or 2.08 percent to 91.219 points on volume of 38.678 million shares worth $22.391 million.
Domestic investors bought heavily into smaller Pudong property shares which are now looking cheap compared to market giant Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development, brokers said.
They said market sentiment appeared to be strengthening.
"Active buying in Pudong shares overwhelmed some unwinding selling ahead of the long Labour Day holiday, which boosted market sentiment," one broker said.
"If there is no negative news during the holiday, the index will test 100 points after the holiday," another broker said.
Pudong real estate firm Shanghai Waigaoqiao Free Trade Zone Development was the star on domestic buying, surging $0.056 or 9.15 percent to $0.668 on volume of 3.0 million shares.
Shanghai Kaikai Industrial was the most actively traded on institutional window-dressing buying, jumping $0.030 or 6.52 percent to $0.490 on volume of 3.6 million shares.
The Shenzhen B share index rose 0.38 point or 0.21 percent to end at 176.27 on turnover of HK$149.9 million.
"The glaringly bad company results did not shock investors because they had expected poor earnings from those companies," an analyst at J&A Securities said.

Shenzhen Tellus Holdings Co Ltd, Hainan Pearl River Enterprises Holdings Ltd and Gintian Industry (Group) Co Ltd all announced losses for 1996 on Wednesday, the final day of the corporate results reporting season.
A handful of other B share companies also announced weaker 1996 earnings compared with 1995.
Conglomerate Tellus ended 3.90 percent higher at HK$3.20 after plunging to its 10 percent limit-down at HK$2.77 within the first few minutes of afternoon trading.
The company on Wednesday announced the sale of its state shares, amounting to 72.4 percent of its equity, to a state-owned company in Shenzhen.
"Investors are expecting improvements in the company's operations this year following the change in shareholding," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
"But it also looks like some big players are manipulating share prices," the J&A analyst said.
Conglomerate Shenzhen Gintian Industry was the biggest loser, falling HK$0.25 or 6.56 percent to HK$3.56.
Shanghai's A share index ended firmer on active selective buying with market sentiment bullish, brokers said.

The index rose 17.417 points or 1.21 percent to 1,456.503 points on volume of 757.6 million shares worth 10.2 billion yuan. The SSE30 blue chip index closed up 45.105 points or 1.14 percent to 3,989.350 points.
The Shenzhen A share index gained 4.50 points or 0.93 percent to end at 489.22 on turnover of 11.7 billion yuan against Tuesday's 14.9 billion.
